questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.**

Bobo was / very richer than Jim / as he had illicitly accumulated / all his wealth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'very richer than Jim'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'richer'** is already in a comparative degree of adjective.
 
• So adding the adjective **'very'** before it is just redundant.
 
• Hence this part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *Bobo was richer than Jim as he had illicitly accumulated all his wealth.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **'Very' **can be used as an adverb (before adjectives and adverbs).
 
• **Example- **
 
 
• It had been a long day and he was **very** tired. 
 
• I always walk **very** quickly. 
 
• She writes **very** well. 
 
 
 
• It can also be used as an adjective (only before a noun).
 
 
• Example- They went down to the** very** bottom of the sea.

questions.question:
**Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully:**

Estella had hardly heard the news (after) she began to weep.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'when'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We use 'when' to introduce a single completed event that takes place in the middle of a longer activity or event. In these cases, we usually use a continuous verb in the main clause to describe the background event.

 
 
• Example- He was walking back to his flat when he heard an explosion.
 
 
 
• 'Hardly' is followed by 'when'.
 
 
• Example: Hardly had I reached the station when the train came.​
 
 
 
• So this is the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed word.​

Correct Sentence: *Estella had hardly heard the news when she began to weep.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• We can use 'while' to talk about two longer events or activities happening at the same time.
 
• We can use either simple or continuous verb forms.
 
 
• Example- We spent long evenings talking in my sitting room while he played the music he had chosen and explained his ideas.
 
 
 
• We can use 'well' when we want to change what we have said slightly, or say something in another way.
 
 
• ​Example- I'm not going on a hiking holiday. Well, I hate being out in the cold weather.​

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Luckily, the machinery was not used by them.

options.text: Luckily, they had not used the machinery.
Luckily, they did not use the machinery.
Luckily, they have not used the machinery.
Luckily, I did not used the machinery.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Luckily, they did not use the machinery.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Point__**

 
• Rules to be followed while converting active voice from passive voice :
 
• Identify the Subject, Verb, and Object in the passive sentence to convert to active voice.
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other i.e. subject of the passive sentence becomes the object in an active sentence.
 
• The past participle (V3) forms in a passive sentence i.e. preceded by (by, with, to, etc) are changed to the base verb in the active sentence.
 
• **'Them'** will be changed to **'they'** as it will become the subject of the active voice.
 
• **Structure:**
 
• Passive Voice - Object + was/were + not + V3 + by + Subject.
 
• Active Voice - Subject + did/do + not + V1 + Object.
 
• Following the above-mentioned rules, the right active sentence: Luckily, they did not use the machinery.
